- .github/workflows/ci.yml:483-522, 922-998 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=[3]

  WHY: The cited job duration changed by only four seconds after #7250’s move, and remaining steps include the heal pytest invocation at line 922 and validation and plan steps from line 924 onward; if those are the slow part, the job remains near its 20-minute cancellation limit and budget-watch issues continue.
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:31, 486-522 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: `static-checks` has the smallest timeout at 15 minutes and receives more test steps despite the issue asking for the job with the most headroom.
  WHY: If the moved steps take several minutes, the job may exceed the 11.25-minute budget-watch threshold or hit its 15-minute timeout; the check-run context did not confirm their durations.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "Move its slowest steps (see the run's step timings) into the CI job with the most headroom, unchanged, keeping job and step names."
  Expected change site: the comment and step placement at .github/workflows/ci.yml lines 483-522. The choice of steps should rest on step timings from run 38481381592 and a headroom comparison between jobs.
  Evidence of absence: The only evidence cited is the job-level "15m04s of its 20 minutes". The diff names no per-step duration and no durations for the other jobs. The #7250 move cited 15m08s for the same job and the job still measured 15m04s afterwards, so selecting steps without timings has already failed once. The slow-step candidates left behind include the heal pytest invocation at line 922 and the steps from line 924 onward. Unless the author can show the moved steps account for the time, the requirement is only partly met.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:26-29 | severity=NIT | confidence=[4]

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:31, 480-522, 528/904/1006 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The PR moves validation test steps into `static-checks`, which has the smallest timeout and budget-watch headroom, contrary to the stated rationale.
  WHY: The 75% threshold gives `static-checks` 11.25 minutes versus 15 minutes for the 20-minute `tests-*` jobs; if the moved steps take nontrivial time, the job may warn or time out. The prior move under #7250 targeted the same job, and the next budget incident (#7334) indicates it did not buy durable headroom.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "Move its slowest steps (see the run's step timings) into the CI job with the most headroom, unchanged, keeping job and step names."
  Expected change site: .github/workflows/ci.yml lines 483-485 (comment justifying the move) and lines 919-924 (steps left behind in tests-heal-plan-and-validation).
  Evidence of absence: The diff cites only the job-level "15m04s of its 20 minutes"; no per-step timing and no headroom comparison across jobs is included. The linked issue summary itself notes live step timings were unavailable. The prior move under #7250 moved different steps to the same target (static-checks), and the very next budget incident (#7334) shows the prior move did not shorten tests-heal-plan-and-validation below the budget threshold. Steps left behind include "Workflow failure heal contract and driver tests" at lines 919-924, which runs `tests/test_workflow_failure_heal.py`, `tests/test_workflow_failure_heal_pr_reconcile.py`, `tests/test_heal_isolated_editor.py`, `tests/test_workflow_failure_heal_scope_tests.py`, `tests/test_provider_outage.py`, and `tests/test_review_autofix_provider_outage_contract.py`. `static-checks` has timeout-minutes: 15 (line 31) versus 20 for the tests-* jobs, so its budget-watch headroom is 11.25 minutes versus 15 minutes for tests-*.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:27-29, 480-522 | severity=NIT | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The header comment’s “About 2 minutes measured” estimate no longer describes `static-checks` after this PR adds ~33 test invocations on top of the ~31 added under #7250.
  WHY: Maintainers may keep treating the job as the cheapest to grow, pushing it past its 11.25-minute warning threshold or 15-minute timeout; nothing is enforced at runtime.
